canonical_name: SVAMP (Simple Variations on Arithmetic Math word Problems), Patel, Bhattamishra & Goyal, NAACL 2021
metric: accuracy (% of problems with correct numeric answer)
ab_system: GPT-4 with Complex-CoT prompting, greedy (90.5); same paper GPT-4 + Progressive-Hint Prompting 91.9
ab_mode: pass@1 greedy, few-shot Complex CoT (PHP variant: iterative self-hinting, still single model)
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.09797 (Progressive-Hint Prompting, arXiv v1 2023-04; Table 8: GPT-4 Complex CoT 90.5 -> PHP 91.9; abstract: 'state-of-the-art performances on SVAMP (89.1% -> 91.9%)')
strict_system: GPT-4 (Complex CoT, greedy), run by third-party researchers
score_at_release_system: Graph2Tree with RoBERTa embeddings (trained on MAWPS+ASDiv-A)
lineage: Parents: ASDiv-A / MAWPS (seed problems varied by the authors, 2021-03). Contemporaries/successors in grade-school math: GSM8K (2021-10); GSM-Plus, GSM-Symbolic (robustness-style successors).
best_by_cutoff: 94.2 — GPT-4 + DUP prompting (arXiv 2404.14963, 2024-04; zero-shot CoT GPT-4 90.4 in same paper); best found, later frontier models rarely report SVAMP
notes: No human baseline in the paper (checked NAACL PDF), so criterion B. Prior SOTA before the event was 89.1 (PoT + self-consistency with Codex, arXiv 2211.12588, 2022-11; self-consistency code-davinci-002 86.8, 2022-03), as the PHP abstract states; no >=90 result found before 2023-04. The PHP paper's arXiv id (2304.) fixes v1 to April 2023; the v1 PDF already contains GPT-4 Table 8. Lab reports: PaLM 540B 8-shot CoT (2022-04, score not parsed), Llama 2-Chat+calculator 69.2 (2023-07), DeepSeek-Coder PAL 71.6 (2023-11). Last lab report 2023-11-02. Wayback/PapersWithCode were not reachable from this environment, so SOTA-history check relied on papers' stated prior SOTA.

canonical_name: SciCode: A Research Coding Benchmark Curated by Scientists (Tian et al., NeurIPS 2024 D&B)
metric: Main Problem Resolve Rate (%), standard setting without scientist background (subproblem resolve rate is the secondary, greyed column)
score_at_release_system: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (main problems, no background; arXiv v1 abstract)
n_items: 80 main problems / 338 subproblems (test split 65 main problems; 15 main problems validation)
lineage: No successor version found by cutoff; integrated into inspect_ai (2025-01) and OpenCompass; used by Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (subproblem-level scoring).
best_by_cutoff: Official leaderboard (main-problem metric): 10.8 — OpenAI o3-mini-low (leaderboard update 2025-02-01/03, github.com/scicode-bench/SciCode README). Lab self-reports (subproblem-level, AA-style): 59 — Gemini 3.1 Pro Thinking High (model card 2026-02-19); Kimi K3 58.7 (2026-07-16).
notes: Creators' headline metric is the main-problem resolve rate (bold on the leaderboard); lab numbers of 44.8-59 are almost certainly the subproblem-level score popularised by Artificial Analysis, not main-problem rate — either way far below 90. No human solve baseline (FAQ: validators reviewed problems, did not solve them; GPT-4 used for reproduction). Official leaderboard last updated 2025-02-03 (site repo commits: only formatting fixes 2025-10-29), but labs kept reporting through 2026-07, so not abandoned.

canonical_name: SealQA (Pham et al., Virginia Tech; ICLR 2026) — coded on its headline split Seal-0 (all lab reports use Seal-0)
metric: accuracy (% correct, graded by GPT-4o-mini auto-rater adapted from SimpleQA grader) on Seal-0, with search tools as part of the task
human_baseline: 38.8 (open search; 50.4 with oracle docs) — measured on 50 Seal-Hard questions, not on Seal-0
score_at_release_system: OpenAI o3 with search, best reasoning effort (arXiv v1 abstract; o4-mini 6.3)
lineage: Family: Seal-0 (core) ⊂ Seal-Hard; LongSeal (long-context distractor variant). Grader inherited from SimpleQA (2024-10). Related: BrowseComp (2025-04), FreshQA (same lab group lineage).
best_by_cutoff: 57.4 — Kimi K2.5 (thinking, avg@4, with tools; self-report 2026-01, github.com/MoonshotAI). Third-party: Parallel Task API Ultra8x 56.8 (parallel.ai blog 2025-11-03); GPT-5-high 43.2 in the paper's updated table.
notes: Unit coded as Seal-0 because every lab report (Kimi K2 Thinking 56.3, Kimi K2.5 57.4, Qwen3.5 46.9) is on Seal-0; codebook rule 1.6 would make Seal-Hard a separate unit if reported. Human baseline exists only on a 50-question Seal-Hard sample and is far below 85%, so B. Tools (web search) are part of the intended protocol, so tool-assisted results count. Maintainers commit to 'review and update its answers regularly' (time-sensitive answers), so scores across paper versions are not strictly comparable (o3: 17.1 in v1 abstract vs 14.4 in later table). llm-stats.com lists only self-reports, max 57.4.

canonical_name: SimpleQA: Measuring short-form factuality in large language models (OpenAI; Wei et al.)
metric: Correct (% of all 4,326 questions graded CORRECT by the prompted ChatGPT grader), closed-book/no browsing. This is the creators' headline number (blog chart Correct/Not attempted/Incorrect; openai/simple-evals 'SimpleQA' column = overall correct). Paper also offers F-score (harmonic mean of correct and correct-given-attempted) as an optional single number.
score_at_release_system: OpenAI o1-preview, no browsing (Correct 42.7; F-score 44.8); GPT-4o 38.2, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 28.9
lineage: Successors/variants: Chinese SimpleQA (Alibaba, arXiv 2411.07140, 2024-11; separate benchmark); BrowseComp (OpenAI, 2025-04-10; browsing successor); SimpleQA Verified (Google DeepMind, arXiv 2509.07968, 2025-09; 1,000 cleaned items, F1 headline). Grader reused by SealQA etc.
best_by_cutoff: Closed-book (counted protocol): 62.5 — GPT-4.5 preview (OpenAI blog/simple-evals, 2025-02-27); no closed-book result >=90 found. Tool-assisted (not counted): 97.1 — DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp agentic search (github 2025-09-29); Grok 4 Fast with search 95.0 (2025-09-19).
notes: Standard protocol is closed-book: blog says OpenAI measured 'several OpenAI models without browsing'; SimpleQA Verified paper also states tools give near-perfect performance and must not be used. Tool-assisted >=90 results therefore NOT counted for AB: earliest found Perplexity Deep Research 93.9% (perplexity.ai blog 2025-02-14); OpenAI GPT-4o Search Preview 90.0 (2025-03); ChatGPT agent 91.4 (2025-07-17); DeepSeek-V3.1 search agent 93.4 (2025-08-21). No human performance baseline: the 94.4% is a third AI trainer's agreement in the data-quality check (est. ~3% label error), not a baseline. JUDGEMENT CALL (C rejected): OpenAI's BrowseComp post (2025-04-10) says 'Existing benchmarks like SimpleQA, which measure models' ability to retrieve basic isolated facts, are already saturated by models with access to fast browsing tools, such as GPT-4o with browsing.' Not coded as C because the saturation claim is explicitly about the tool-assisted (non-counting) protocol and OpenAI kept reporting closed-book SimpleQA afterwards (GPT-5 system card 2025-08, gpt-oss-safeguard 2025-10-29); if adjudicators read it as C, c_date=2025-04, source https://openai.com/index/browsecomp/. E not coded: SimpleQA Verified (Google, 2025-09) reports noisy labels/redundancy and drops 76.9% of items, but mostly for de-duplication, publisher and topic balancing; removals for source conflicts are 8.3% + 3.9% of the remaining pool, so a >=20% defect rate is not documented, although Google, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Meta moved to SimpleQA Verified from 2025-11. Lab-report parsing: C-SimpleQA/CSimpleQA lines (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen) are Chinese SimpleQA, a different benchmark; 'Hallucination rate' lines are a lower-is-better sub-metric. Last report of original SimpleQA by a listed lab: 2025-10-29 (OpenAI gpt-oss-safeguard), <12 months before cutoff, so not abandoned.

canonical_name: SimpleQA Verified: A Reliable Factuality Benchmark to Measure Parametric Knowledge (Haas et al., Google DeepMind/Google Research)
metric: F1-score = harmonic mean of overall correct and correct-given-attempted (creators' headline; Kaggle leaderboard metric), no tools
lineage: Parent: SimpleQA (OpenAI, 2024-10; 4,326 items) filtered by de-duplication, topic/answer-type balancing, publisher opt-out and source reconciliation to 1,000 items, with an improved autorater prompt. No successor by cutoff.
best_by_cutoff: 72.1 — Gemini 3 Pro ('state-of-the-art 72.1% on SimpleQA Verified', blog.google 2025-11-18); a secondary blog lists Gemini 3.1 Pro at 75.6 (not confirmed in Google's 3.1 Pro model card). Meta Muse Spark 70.8 (2026-04-08).
notes: Closed-book protocol is explicit: 'Enabling tools on SimpleQA Verified results in near perfect performance, emphasizing that SimpleQA Verified should be employed for measuring parametric factuality only' (arXiv v2), so tool-assisted runs would not count. No human baseline -> B. Lab reports do not always state whether the number is F1 or accuracy (Google reports a single %; DeepSeek labels 'Pass@1'/'EM'; DeepSeek V4.1-Flash 42.3 is a 25-shot base-model EM); all are far below 90 either way. Kaggle leaderboard not machine-readable from this environment (blocked); best_by_cutoff relies on lab announcements.

canonical_name: SuperGPQA: Scaling LLM Evaluation across 285 Graduate Disciplines (M-A-P / ByteDance Seed)
metric: accuracy, Overall (sample-level) over 26,529 multiple-choice questions (~9.67 options each)
lineage: Inspired by GPQA (2023-11) / GPQA Diamond; broad-coverage successor in the MMLU-Pro/GPQA line. No successor version by cutoff (repo: 3 questions fixed 2025-04-30).
best_by_cutoff: 73.6 — Qwen3.7-Max (Alibaba blog, self-report 2026-05-20); Seed 2.1 Pro 70.8 (self-report, llm-stats). Official HF leaderboard (m-a-p/SuperGPQA) not readable here.
notes: No human/expert answering baseline reported (checked arXiv HTML), so B (90). Creators' leaderboard metric is Overall (sample) accuracy; subfield/field/discipline-averaged variants are secondary. Lab reports mix chat/thinking models (57-73.6) and 5-shot base-model EM (DeepSeek V4 53.9, V4.1-Flash 53.1); none near 90. Questions annotated by 80+ experts with Human-LLM collaborative filtering (curation coded expert-written).

canonical_name: TheoremQA: A Theorem-driven Question Answering dataset (Chen et al., EMNLP 2023)
metric: accuracy (% exact answer match; answers are float/integer/bool/list/option)
human_baseline: 80 (mean of four undergraduates on 20 random questions: 12/20, 15/20, 18/20, 19/20); authors say expert level should be ~100
abandoned_evidence: Last report by a listed lab: Qwen2.5 technical report (Alibaba, 2024-12-19, TheoremQA 42.4 for Qwen2.5-72B base); no listed lab reported it in the following 12+ months. Official leaderboard (HF space TIGER-Lab/Science-Leaderboard): results.csv last updated 2024-05-05 (huggingface.co/datasets/wenhu/science_leaderboard_submission commits), space last commit 2024-06-30, space now fails with a runtime error; GitHub repos wenhuchen/TheoremQA and TIGER-AI-Lab/TheoremQA last commits 2024-04/05. Both 12-month conditions met by 2025-12.
score_at_release_system: GPT-4 with Program-of-Thoughts (51% in abstract; leaderboard 52.4; GPT-4 CoT 43.8)
lineage: Part of TIGER-Lab Science Leaderboard (2024-04) alongside MMLU-STEM/GPQA; no successor version. Related: TheoremExplainBench (TIGER-Lab, 2025).
best_by_cutoff: 59.1 — DeepSeek-R1, run independently in General-Reasoner paper (TIGER-Lab, arXiv 2505.14652, 2025-05); o1-mini 53.1, GPT-4o 43.6 in same table. Best listed-lab self-report: Qwen2-72B-Instruct 44.4 (2024-06).
notes: Human baseline (80% on a 20-question sample, 4 students) is <85% and on a sample, so B (90). Never close to 90 by the cutoff. Abandonment uses the codebook rule (listed labs + leaderboard); third-party papers kept using TheoremQA in 2025 (e.g., General-Reasoner), which the rule does not count. Only Alibaba/Qwen ever reported it (5 releases). 53 of the 800 questions include images (theoremqa_visual_subset_test.json); modality coded text.

exclusion_reason: Measures truthfulness, i.e. the tendency to avoid imitative falsehoods. The creators' primary objective is '% of answers that are true', and non-committal answers ('I have no comment') count as true, so the metric can be maximised by abstaining (README). Labs file it under safety/honesty: Llama 2 next to ToxiGen/BOLD, Claude 2 under honesty. Inverse scaling with model size in the original paper.
canonical_name: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods (Lin, Hilton & Evans, ACL 2022)
metric: Generation (main task): % true (primary) and % true-and-informative (secondary), judged by humans or fine-tuned GPT-judge; MC1/MC2 multiple-choice variants; binary-choice variant added Jan 2025
human_baseline: 94 (% true); 87 (% true and informative) — one participant, 250 randomly sampled questions, ~2 min/question, internet allowed
lineage: MC1/MC2 multiple-choice variants (2021); new binary-choice version recommended by the authors (README update Jan 2025: 'We recommend this new version over the original multiple-choice versions ... previous results on MC1 and MC2 are still valid'). Translated TruthfulQA used in GPT-4o system card.
notes: JUDGEMENT CALL (stratum). Coded as propensity because the README defines the primary objective as % true and admits it 'can be gamed with a model that responds "I have no comment" to every question'. If adjudicated as main: primary metric = % true (generation), human baseline 94 on a 250-question random sample of the same set, so criterion A with threshold 94 (or 87 if % true-and-informative is taken as primary); MC1/MC2 have no human baseline, so B=90. Event research was not done, per the instruction to stop at identification for non-main strata. Jan 2025 authors' update is not a C event: old MC results are declared 'still valid'. Lab-report parsing: GPT-4o 81.4 is MC accuracy on English Translated TruthfulQA; Llama 2-Chat 64.14 and Code Llama 34.64/47.37 are % true-and-informative; InstructGPT 0.712 is % true with QA prompt.

canonical_name: 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad (54th USAMO), 6 proof problems; LLM evaluation protocol of MathArena 'Proof or Bluff' (human-graded proofs, 7 pts/problem)
release_source: https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/2025_USAMO ('held on March 19 and March 20, 2025'); MAA report https://campus.lakeforest.edu/trevino/USAMO2025.pdf
metric: % of 42 points (6 problems x 7), proofs graded by expert human judges (MathArena: mean over 4 runs)
abandoned_evidence: Last report by a listed lab: xAI Grok 4 launch 2025-07-09 ('Grok 4 Heavy leads USAMO'25 with 61.9%', https://x.ai/news/grok-4); none found afterwards (Anthropic reports USAMO 2026 from 2026-04). MathArena USAMO 2025 leaderboard: HF dataset MathArena/usamo_2025_outputs holds only 10 models, the latest DeepSeek-R1-0528 (released 2025-05-28), so no new entries after mid-2025; the dataset file was re-uploaded 2026-09-11 without new models. MathArena's 2026 post (2026-03-28) refers to USAMO 2025 only as last year's baseline. 12 months without lab reports or leaderboard activity reached 2026-07, before the cutoff.
score_at_release_system: Gemini 2.5 Pro (MathArena, 10.1/42 ≈ 24%, 'non-trivial score of 25%'; all other models <5%), evaluated within ~1-2 weeks of the exam (arXiv 2503.21934)
lineage: USAMO annual series: USAMO 2024 (MathArena config) -> USAMO 2025 -> USAMO 2026 (2026-03). Evaluation harness: MathArena 'Proof or Bluff' (arXiv 2503.21934, v1 2025-03-27).
best_by_cutoff: 61.9 — Grok 4 Heavy (xAI self-report, 2025-07-09, https://x.ai/news/grok-4); Gemini 2.5 Deep Think 49.4 (Google I/O self-report, 2025-05-20). MathArena independent max well below 50 (only 16 of 240 graded runs scored >=0.9).
notes: No human baseline set by MAA/MathArena (308 contestants; mean not published in the MAA draft report), so B (90% = 37.8/42). No >=90 result found by the cutoff; formal (Lean) provers would use a verifier tool and not count for this no-tools proof exam anyway. Abandonment depends on no listed lab reporting USAMO 2025 after 2025-07-09 (input D3 matrix agrees: last_lab_report 2025-07-09); medium confidence because self-reports in later cards could have been missed.

canonical_name: 2026 USA Mathematical Olympiad, 6 proof problems; MathArena USAMO 2026 evaluation (LLM-jury grading with full human review)
metric: % of 42 points (6 problems x 7), mean over 4 runs per problem (MathArena)
ab_mode: mean of 4 runs per problem (pass@1 average); LLM-jury grading checked by hand
ab_source: https://matharena.ai/usamo/ (MathArena post 2026-03-28, Table 1: GPT-5.4 95.2%, Gemini-3.1-Pro 74.4%, Opus-4.6 47.0%)
score_at_release_system: GPT-5.4 (xhigh), MathArena, published 2026-03-28 (6 days after the exam)
lineage: USAMO annual series: USAMO 2025 (2025-03; best 61.9) -> USAMO 2026. Evaluated by MathArena (NeurIPS D&B 2025); Anthropic self-reports use MathArena grading.
best_by_cutoff: 99.8 — Claude Mythos 5 (Anthropic system card self-report 2026-06-09, per input lab-report line; not independently confirmed). Claude Mythos Preview 97.6 (self-report 2026-04-07); independent best: GPT-5.4 xhigh 95.2 (MathArena 2026-03-28).
notes: The first independent evaluation, 6 days after the exam, already exceeds 90%, so born_saturated=1 (event month = release month). Anthropic's 97.6 (Mythos Preview, 2026-04-07) came later. MathArena graded with an LLM jury (GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Opus-4.6) and reviewed every solution by hand ('After Human Intervention' column). No human baseline published, so B. The MathArena repo config dates the competition '2026-03-22'.

canonical_name: Virology Capabilities Test (VCT): A Multimodal Virology Q&A Benchmark (SecureBio / CAIS; Götting et al.)
metric: accuracy (% of questions with the exact correct set of true statements; multiple-response, 4-10 statements per question)
direction: higher is better (capability measure; hazardous-capability proxy)
human_baseline: 22.1 (expert virologists with internet, on questions in their own sub-areas)
score_at_release_system: OpenAI o3 (arXiv v1 abstract; 'outperforming 94% of expert virologists')
lineage: Successor: VCT-v2 (SecureBio, 2026-09-11; 279 questions, 'more shortcut-resistant, more accurate, and further ahead of saturation'); v1 kept alongside v2. Sister SecureBio evals used by labs: HPCT, WCB, ReproBAIT.
best_by_cutoff: 67.4 — Grok 4.6 (high), xAI model card self-report 2026-08-12 (xAI scoring may differ). Creator-run: GPT-5.6 Sol 53.9 on VCT v1 (SecureBio VCT-v2 post, 2026-09-11).
notes: Expert baseline 22.1% is far below 85%, so B (90). Dataset is gated: 'freely available upon request to any organization with a track record of working on biosecurity and/or AI safety' (securebio.org), so coded private-heldout. Lab system cards referenced SecureBio's multimodal virology eval before the paper (Anthropic Claude 3.7 Sonnet card 2025-02-24); birth set at the creators' first public release (arXiv 2025-04) per the rules. Not a C event: the VCT-v2 post says 'While VCT is not saturated at the time of this writing ... we may be only a few model generations away from VCT's effective ceiling' and keeps v1 for comparison. Self-reported numbers vary with scoring (OpenAI 'refusal-corrected accuracy' 57.8; Anthropic 0.574; Meta 49.7/52.0; xAI 54.5-67.4); all well below 90.

canonical_name: The WMDP Benchmark (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy): WMDP-Bio, WMDP-Chem, WMDP-Cyber (Li et al., CAIS/Scale AI; ICML 2024)
metric: zero-shot 4-option MCQ accuracy, no tools; for the whole unit: size-weighted overall accuracy over all 3,668 questions (lm-eval-harness 'wmdp' group). Creators publish no single headline number, only per-subset accuracies.
direction: higher is better (more hazardous-knowledge capability; for unlearning use lower is desired, but the unit is coded as a capability benchmark as labs use it)
lineage: Dataset revised 2024-03-08 (Cyber choice randomisation) and 2024-04-23 (malformed/overlong/non-dual-use items removed; 4,157 -> 3,668 items, ~12%). Related/successor bio evals: VCT (SecureBio, 2025-04; VCT-v2 2026-09); the VCT-v2 post reports shortcut exploitation in >30% of WMDP-Bio questions.
best_by_cutoff: Overall (computed): 89.5 — Grok 4.6 high (xAI model card 2026-08-12: Bio 90.0 / Chem 85.3 / Cyber 90.1). Per subset: Bio 91 Grok 4.20 (2026-02-17); Chem 87.3 Grok 4.5 (2026-07-16); Cyber 90.1 Grok 4.6 (2026-08-12).
notes: JUDGEMENT CALL (metric for a multi-subset unit): creators give only per-subset scores, so the unit is coded on overall accuracy across the three named subsets (the harness group score), computed from self-reports when all three are given. No overall >=90 is documented by the cutoff (Grok 4.6 = 89.5; Grok 4.7 = 87.7), so alive. If adjudicators use WMDP-Bio as the headline: first no-tools Bio >=90 = Grok 4.20 single-agent 0.91 (xAI system card 2026-02-17, self-report). OpenAI deep research's 90% (system card 2025-02-25) used browsing (87% without; o1 86%, o3-mini 86%) on a 1,520-question Bio set, so it does not count under the no-tools rule. Cyber >=90 first Grok 4.6 90.1 (2026-08). No human baseline, so B. Not E: OpenAI says it 'consider[s] it contaminated' because it is published (generic caveat, no evidence); a longest-option heuristic scores 0.465 on WMDP-Bio (github.com/saanviiyer/palimpsest), not near ceiling. Codebook rule 1.6 would make WMDP-Bio/Chem/Cyber separate units if the study splits them.

canonical_name: WildBench v2: Benchmarking LLMs with Challenging Tasks from Real Users in the Wild (Lin et al., AI2; ICLR 2025)
release_source: HF space allenai/WildBench commit 'init design for v2 leaderboard' 2024-05-26 (huggingface.co/spaces/allenai/WildBench/commits/main?p=3); arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04770 v1 2024-06-07. WildBench v1 leaderboard launched 2024-03-06.
metric: WB-Score: checklist-guided 1-10 rating by an LLM judge (GPT-4-Turbo in the paper), rescaled S'=(S-5)x2 and shown x10, range -80..100. Paired metric WB-Reward (pairwise vs reference models, -100..100). Leaderboard default sort is WB-Elo (LC), which has no ceiling.
score_at_release_system: GPT-4o-2024-05-13 (WB-Score; WB-Reward mix 35.7), arXiv v1 Table 2
lineage: WildBench v1 (leaderboard 2024-03-06, pairwise GPT-4 arena-style eval) -> WildBench v2 (2024-05/06; WB-Reward with 3 references + checklists, WB-Score; WB-Elo added 2024-06-16). Tasks mined from WildChat logs. Same group's ZeroEval/ZebraLogic.
best_by_cutoff: 68.5 — Mistral Large 3 / Ministral 3 14B Instruct 2512 (Mistral self-report, HF model card 2025-12-02; judge setup may differ from the official one). Official leaderboard (frozen 2024-08-06): top WB-Score 58.8 for gpt-4o-2024-05-13 in data_dir/all_stat_wildbench.-1.jsonl.
notes: JUDGEMENT CALL (stratum): the leaderboard ranks by WB-Elo (LC) by default (app.py), which would point to excluded:no_ceiling. Kept as main because the paper's two defined metrics (WB-Score, WB-Reward) are bounded and every lab report uses WB-Score. Unit coded as v2, the version labs report ('Wildbench v2'); v1 (2024-03) used a different protocol. Official leaderboard inactive since 2024-08-06, but Mistral kept self-reporting (Small 3.2 2025-06-20: 65.33; Ministral 3 / Large 3 2025-12-02: 68.5), so it is less than 12 months since the last lab report: alive, not abandoned. Input list ends at 2025-06-20 and misses the Dec-2025 Mistral reports. Mistral's numbers likely use a GPT-4o judge (per its cards), not directly comparable with the GPT-4-Turbo-judged leaderboard. No human baseline.

canonical_name: WritingBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Generative Writing (Wu et al., Alibaba / X-PLUG)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05244 (v1 2025-03-07); github.com/X-PLUG/WritingBench README '2025-03-10 We release the first version of WritingBench, including 1,239 writing queries'
metric: mean rubric score: 5 query-specific criteria per query, each scored 1-10 by a judge (paper: fine-tuned Qwen-7B critic; leaderboard: Claude-3.7-Sonnet from 2025-04-29, Claude-Sonnet-4 from 2025-09-05, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 from 2025-11-27). Leaderboard multiplies by 10 (0-100).
score_at_release_system: DeepSeek-R1, critic-model judge, original 1,239-query version (arXiv v1 Table 3; Qwen-Max 8.37, ChatGPT-4o-latest 8.16)
lineage: v1 2025-03 (1,239 queries, critic model) -> 2025-04-29 revision (1,000 queries, new criteria/prompt, Claude-3.7-Sonnet judge, HF/ModelScope leaderboard) -> judge switched to Claude-Sonnet-4 (2025-09-05) and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 (2025-11-27). No renamed successor.
best_by_cutoff: 88.3 — Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 (Qwen HF card self-report 2025-07-25, Claude-3.7 judge era). Official leaderboard (Sonnet-4.5 judge, imported 2026-05-28 by benchmarklist.com): top gpt-5-2025-08-07 83.87; LongCat 2.0 83.8 (2026-07-20).
notes: Scale: leaderboard 0-100 (raw 10-point score x10), so threshold 90 = 9.0 raw. No human answering baseline; human annotators only validated judge agreement (83%), so B. Nothing >=90 under any judge/version. VERSION CALL: the 2025-04-29 revision changed >10% of items (1,239 -> 1,000 with updated criteria) and the judge, so under codebook rule 1.2 it could be its own unit with birth 2025-04; coded here as one family unit (unversioned name in all lab reports) with birth at first release (2025-03). Qwen3 tech report's 8.03 (2025-05) is on the raw 10-point scale; later Qwen numbers (85.2, 88.3, 87.3) use the leaderboard 100-point scale. Scores across judge changes are not comparable. Lab reports continued past the input list (Qwen3-VL series 2025-09/10; repo and leaderboard updates to 2025-12; leaderboard snapshot 2026-05), so not abandoned.

canonical_name: ZebraLogic (logic grid puzzles; AI2/UW; HF blog 2024-07, ICML 2025 paper 'On the Scaling Limits of LLMs for Logical Reasoning')
release_source: HF leaderboard space allenai/ZebraLogic initial commits 2024-07-11 (huggingface.co/spaces/allenai/ZebraLogic/commits/main); blog https://huggingface.co/blog/yuchenlin/zebra-logic (July 2024); arXiv 2502.01100 v1 2025-02-03
metric: puzzle-level accuracy (% of 1,000 puzzles with every cell correct), greedy decoding; cell-level accuracy is secondary
ab_source: Official ZeroEval/ZebraLogic leaderboard: github.com/WildEval/ZeroEval commit c86a194 'add o3 mini results' 2025-04-01 (result_dirs/zebra-grid.summary.json: Puzzle Acc 91.70); HF space allenai/ZebraLogic summary update 2025-04-01
strict_system: o3-mini-2025-01-31-high, evaluated by the benchmark organizers
score_at_release_system: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (2024-06-20), per the July 2024 blog ('can only solve 33.4% of all puzzles')
lineage: Part of AI2's ZeroEval suite (with WildBench). Paper version 2025-02 (same 1,000 puzzles, adds Z3 search-space analysis). Successor/variant: MultiZebraLogic (arXiv 2511.03553, multilingual).
best_by_cutoff: 97.3 — Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking (Alibaba self-report, 2025-09; via llm-stats); official leaderboard top grok-3-mini-fast-beta-high 92.6 (ZeroEval commit 2025-04-14).
notes: Leaderboard history (git log of result_dirs/zebra-grid.summary.json): top was o1-mini 46.7 (2024-09-13), o1-preview 71.4 (2024-10-22), o1-2024-12-17 81.0 (2025-01-21, also in arXiv v1 2025-02-03), then o3-mini-high 91.7 (2025-04-01), the first >=90; grok-3-mini-fast-beta-high 92.6 followed (2025-04-14). No earlier >=90 found in papers or lab reports (Qwen3 thinking 80.3 in 2025-05; Kimi K2 89.0 and Qwen3-2507 95.0 in 2025-07). No human baseline; blog gives only the author's solve times. Puzzles are generated programmatically (curation synthetic/templated).

canonical_name: ruMMLU (Russian MMLU-style task of the MERA benchmark, Fenogenova et al., ACL 2024; v1.0/1.1 closed test of 961 hand-written questions, 5-shot)
release_source: github.com/ai-forever/MERA commit 12daebd 2023-11-21 'Mera sets, benchmark code and examples' (task table: 'ruMMLU | rummlu | Reasoning | 961 | 5 | acc'); arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04531 v1 2024-01-09
metric: accuracy, 4-option MCQ, 5-shot, on the closed test (labels hidden; scored via the MERA submission system)
human_baseline: 84.4 ('Accuracy of the annotation on the test set', crowd annotators with majority vote). MERA's human-benchmark table lists 0.898, which is the MMLU paper's English expert-level estimate, not measured on this split.
c_source: https://mera.a-ai.ru/en/leaderboard ; https://huggingface.co/datasets/MERA-evaluation/MERA (card last modified 2024-09-24); github.com/MERA-Evaluation/MERA v1.2.0 docs (2024-09-18/19)
c_quote: MERA v1.2.0 leaderboard: 'The previous leaderboard is no longer supported'; scores computed 'excluding public tasks from the computation of the final score'. Dataset card: 'NB that 8 datasets are diagnostic and not used in the overall model evaluation' (ruMMLU among them). The closed MMLU-style test moved to the new MaMuRAMu (4,248 items); ruMMLU became an open 14,012-item machine-translated MMLU.
score_at_release_system: best open baseline in the MERA paper (Mistral, per arXiv 2401.04531 v3 summary); frontier closed models not in the paper
n_items: 961 (closed test, v1.0-1.1); from v1.2.0 'ruMMLU' = 14,012-item public translated MMLU (diagnostic)
lineage: MMLU (2020-09) -> ruMMLU closed test in MERA v1.0/1.1 (2023-11) -> replaced in the scored suite by MaMuRAMu (MERA v1.2.0, 2024-09, 4,248 closed items); the name ruMMLU kept for a public translated-MMLU diagnostic set (14,012). Related: NLP-Core-Team/mmlu_ru, MMMLU.
best_by_cutoff: Not established: MERA leaderboards are JavaScript-rendered and the old v1.1 leaderboard is unsupported; listed-lab reports (Qwen2/2.5, 2024-06 to 2024-12) give ruMMLU only inside a Multi-Exam average.
notes: In the population only via Alibaba/Qwen (4 releases; Qwen2 report cites 'ruMMLU (Fenogenova et al., 2024) (5-shot)' = MERA). Russian-contour benchmark per codebook 2.3, but it meets the 3-release rule. JUDGEMENT CALL: C coded at 2024-09 because the maintainers froze the old leaderboard and removed ruMMLU from the scored suite, replacing its closed test with MaMuRAMu; no explicit saturation reason is stated, so this is a deprecation/freeze reading of C. AB could not be checked: no source with ruMMLU closed-test scores of frontier models found (mera.a-ai.ru not machine-readable; web-search budget exhausted). If an AB >=90 occurred before 2024-09 it would be primary; this seems unlikely given 84.4% annotator accuracy and 2024-era scores, but it is unverified. Without C, the unit would be abandoned (last lab report 2024-12-19; leaderboard unsupported since 2024-09).
